mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% (as of the decision date) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 250 (Dec 2017 base) indicates elevated inflation, prompting market concerns about aggressive monetary tightening, which results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains above 250 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) exceed their respective 12-month moving averages, it signals a robust housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market with unemployment below 4.0% and a decline in unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points over the past three months, the economy is in late-cycle expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0 and UNRATE_3mo_change < -0.2, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 100) signals a weakening economy, which increases the probability of recession and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 100 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (year-over-year) exceeding 2.5% indicates robust economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When the year-over-year GDP growth rate exceeds 2.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) is high while the federal funds rate remains low (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), it signals a risk of stagflation, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS < 1.5, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high industrial production index (INDPRO above 100) signals robust economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 100 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.
